title: Auth API 401/429 debugging scratchpad (Olivia)
content:
Goal: quick breadcrumbs for the intermittent 401 / 429 spike we're seeing in hosted API (mar 2-4). Use as incident notes + runbook input.

Symptoms observed:
- Starting ~2026-03-02 09:40 UTC we saw elevated 401s for a subset of keys and 429s across high-throughput routes.
- 401s are correlated to a particular client_id (client-frontend-42) but not all requests from that client.
- 429s affect multiple clients on the same route and seem correlated with bursty traffic patterns (short spikes).
- Error sample from logs:
  - 2026-03-02T09:42:11Z request_id=abc123 status=401 message="API key not found" api_key_id=sk_live_XXXXX
  - 2026-03-02T09:42:12Z request_id=abc124 status=429 message="rate limit exceeded" limit=1200 window=60

Commands / repro steps tried locally:
1) Repro single 401 from curl (using the same key the customer provided):
   curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_CUSTOM" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
   -> response: 401 {"error":"API key not found"}
   Notes: same key works for some other endpoints (embeddings). Suspect scoping or per-route token restrictions.

2) Throttling repro for 429 (local load test):
   hey -n 5000 -c 200 -q 10 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_TEST" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
   -> saw 429s starting at ~120 rps, matches token-based per-minute window in proxy config.

3) Check quota and key metadata via internal admin API:
   GET /internal/keys/sk_live_CUSTOM -> returned key object with fields (scope: ["embed"], status: active, created_by: frontend-team)
   -> Scope was limited to embeddings only (ah). So 401 expected on generation endpoint.

4) Checked rotation timeline:
   - Customer rotated keys on 2026-03-01 22:10 UTC. Old key deactivated 2026-03-01 22:15 UTC.
   - Provided key in incident is a post-rotation key but appears to have only embed scope.

Hypotheses:
- 401s: caused by key scoping mismatch (embed-only key used for generate route) OR accidental use of a revoked/staged key.
- 401s intermittent: maybe there are multiple keys in the client app and a subset of requests use the wrong key (race / config bug).
- 429s: standard per-key or per-route rate-limit being hit due to short bursts; our proxy enforces both per-key and per-route windows.
- 429 burst behavior: batching and client retries (exponential backoff missing) amplify bursts leading to crossing the window boundary.

Immediate action items done:
- Reached out to customer (frontend) to confirm which key was in use (they confirmed config has two env vars; one still set to old embed-only key).
- Updated internal admin to temporarily bump per-key qps for their org to reduce 429s while they fix client backoff (change ephemeral; will revert).
- Added a log trigger to flag when a key that lists only embed scope hits a non-embed endpoint (alert rule: embed-scope-misuse).

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- Team: eng-serving-runtime to add 1) clearer 403 vs 401 differentiation in proxy (401=missing/invalid key, 403=valid key but insufficient scope) and 2) log full key_scope in audit logs (redact key id).
- Product: notify customers when they rotate keys about potential scope mismatches (small doc blurb in rotation flow).
- SRE: evaluate whether short-window smoothing (leaky bucket across seconds) will reduce 429 spikes for bursty clients without increasing cost.
- Docs: write short runbook for customers describing how to check key scopes and how to interpret 401 vs 429 responses.

Notes on headers and telemetry to check next:
- Check upstream proxy (envoy) response headers for rate-limit metadata: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Customer reported not seeing these; verify proxy config includes inject.
- Look at traces: correlate request_id to edge logs, auth-service decision, and quota-service evaluation.
- Audit auth-service logs for key lookup failures: timing, cache misses (redis), and fallback to DB. Suspect a cache TTL misconfiguration could cause transient 401s if lookups fail under load.

Commands to run (internal):
- Query key scopes: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://internal.redwood.ai/v1/keys/sk_live_CUSTOM
- Rate-limit stats for org: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://internal.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/ORG-42/ratelimits
- Edge logs (bigquery): SELECT * FROM edge_logs WHERE request_time BETWEEN '2026-03-02T09:40:00Z' AND '2026-03-02T09:45:00Z' AND status IN (401,429) LIMIT 1000

Incident blameless note:
- Root cause looks like a combination of customer misconfiguration (embed-only key) and our UX not making scope mismatches obvious. Also proxy throttling behavior amplifies bursts. Plan is not to blame the customer; fix UX + telemetry + smoothing.

Estimated fix timeline:
- Short-term (hours): revert temp qps bump, add embed-scope-misuse alert, customer fix keys.
- Mid-term (1-2 weeks): proxy response header consistency, adjust error codes, add runbook.
- Long-term (quarter): evaluate quota smoothing and more flexible burst handling; consider per-org burst buffers.

Open items / questions:
- Do we have any other customers with similar embed-only misconfigurations? (scan list of keys with scope mismatch)
- Can we make rotation flow warn if new key scopes differ from previous?

Slack refs: see thread #infra-auth (link above). Linear ticket: RD-1234 (rate limit tweaks + alert).

Scratchy notes / bits to remember: 
- If cache (redis) flaps under load, we might see transient 401s until DB checks succeed. Check redis latency metrics.
- 429 windows: verify whether rate limit uses fixed-minute windows (leading to synchronized resets) vs rolling windows (less spike-prone).
- Add unit tests for scope enforcement middleware to assert correct HTTP status codes for scope mismatch.

---
End of scratchpad. Will update after follow-ups.
